title: 2026 Ballot
intro: Nine Baltimore City questions asked voters to approve borrowing of up to $280 million and to change the city charter. Questions A through D covered borrowing for housing, schools, neighborhood development, and infrastructure. Questions E through I proposed charter changes. Three of them (E, F, and G) would take rules out of the charter or move decisions away from the Board of Estimates, H would create a new Department of Water and Wastewater, and I, placed on the ballot by petition, would create the Baltimore Baby Fund.

title: 2024 Ballot
intro: Eight Baltimore City questions asked voters to approve borrowing of up to $250 million and to make changes to the city charter. Questions A through D covered borrowing for housing, schools, neighborhood development, and infrastructure. Questions E through H proposed charter changes: writing the Police Department into the charter, changing how Inner Harbor shoreline land can be used, creating a fund for the Community Reinvestment and Reparations Commission, and reducing the City Council from 14 districts to 8. Question H was the only one placed on the ballot by petition.
